question: Why is the incident backlog finally dropping?

intro.title: Marcus steps onto the Bridge
intro.text: IT Operations, Singapore. 3,120 endpoints, five sites — and a network-operations console at Mediacorp that reads like a live status board, not a dashboard.

hero.title: Dial, countdown, lamps
hero.text: The uptime dial holds 99.96% above the 99.90 SLO. Beside it, a live countdown to Tuesday 09:00 — 214 endpoints still exposed to CVE-2026-31842.

kpis.title: Four naked numbers
kpis.text: A bare stat strip, sparklines and all: 47 open incidents, uptime 99.96%, patch compliance 96.8%, MTTR 3.4 hours. Straight from ServiceNow and Jira.

chart.title: Correlate: one joined canvas
chart.text: Chapter 01 fuses opened-versus-resolved into a single full-bleed chart. July spiked to 521 opened; August closed 474 against 447 — the backlog finally bends.

ask.title: Drag a lamp, ask why
ask.text: GlobalProtect's lamp burns amber — 84 incidents in 30 days. Marcus drags it into chat and asks the obvious: why is the backlog finally dropping?

delegate.title: Runbooks and dispatch
delegate.text: Chapter 02: cross-app runbooks on the left, a dispatch column on the right — askMElah executes end to end, every hop logged across the stack.

autopilot.title: Triage queue, autopilot on
autopilot.text: Approvals routed like incidents — P1 to P3, SLA lamps blinking. Flip Autopilot and low-risk items like Lena's $3,940 SSD expense clear themselves.

mcp.title: Uplinks: eight of eight
mcp.text: The footer rail reads UPLINKS — ServiceNow, Jira, Slack, GitHub and four more glyphs, 8/8 NOMINAL. One click opens the full MCP console.

recap.title: Recap on demand
recap.text: One button on the board — draft my end-of-week recap — and askMElah compiles the burn-down, patched stragglers and Austin access packs for Priya.

crew.title: The Crew: Patch takes the PO
crew.text: Delegate the Dell PO chase and The Crew opens — Patch, Marcus's agent, carries it to the askMElah hub, hands the payload to Hawk in Procurement, and walks the answer back to his desk.

outro.title: The Bridge holds
outro.text: Same Marcus, same five fires. Now the console watches the lamps and the countdown — while he runs the strategy.
